generic_name: Darunavir, Cobicistat, Emtricitabine, and Tenofovir Alafenamide
drug_class: Combination Antiretroviral (HIV treatment) — includes a protease inhibitor, a pharmacokinetic enhancer, and two nucleoside/nucleotide reverse transcriptase inhibitors
purpose: This medication is used to treat HIV-1 infection in adults and some children. It helps keep the amount of HIV virus in your body very low so your immune system can stay strong. It does not cure HIV, but it helps you live a healthier life and reduces the risk of passing the virus to others.
how_it_works: This pill combines four medicines that attack HIV in different ways. Two of them (emtricitabine and tenofovir alafenamide) block the virus from copying its genetic material inside your cells. Darunavir stops the virus from assembling into new, working copies of itself, and cobicistat is a booster that helps darunavir stay in your body longer and work more effectively.
common_side_effects: Nausea, diarrhea, headache, rash, and stomach upset are the most common side effects. You may also notice tiredness or trouble sleeping. Most side effects are mild and often improve after the first few weeks of treatment.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as stopping can allow HIV to become harder to treat. It can cause serious liver problems, especially if you also have hepatitis B — your doctor will monitor you closely. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you take because this drug has many interactions. Rarely, it can affect your kidneys or cause a buildup of lactic acid, which is a serious condition — contact your doctor if you feel very weak, have unusual muscle pain, or trouble breathing.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one tablet taken by mouth once a day with food. Taking it with a meal helps your body absorb the medicine properly and reduces stomach upset. Try to take it at the same time every day to keep the drug levels steady in your body.
